reviewer: claude-opus-5 acting as the joshi pump-discovery deputy, autonomously, without Ember present
rationale: PROMOTED for /coins. WHY A ROW PROJECTION AND NOT A DOCUMENT FINGERPRINT. schema_fingerprint collapses every array element onto the single pointer $/*, so a page's digest is the UNION of the key sets of whichever coins happened to land in it. Eleven reads of /coins on 2026-08-22 produced EIGHT distinct fingerprints; two byte-identical requests ninety-seven seconds apart differed by exactly cto_address, cto_username and cto_profile_image because one page contained a coin with a community takeover recorded and the other did not. That gate reports on which coins arrived, not on whether the provider changed anything, so it would admit about one read in eight and label the other seven provider drift. This review narrows instead: every row must carry the required leaves in the reviewed wire type, a row may carry the optional leaves, and ANY other leaf refuses the page rather than being silently projected away. Silent projection is exactly how ath_market_cap and volume_1h_usd went missing from three routes for three days without one test going red. The optional set is CLOSED: adding to it is a review act performed by a person writing down what they looked at, never an inference from a body that happened to arrive. The whole-document fingerprint is still recorded on every decision as a drift signal; it simply decides nothing. REVIEWED MATERIAL, as v1 first wrote it down: 26 live response bodies and 1308 rows, all fetched 2026-08-22 through the bounded source-edge client. 36 leaf lines were present on every one of those 1308 rows and are required here; 31 more appeared on some rows and not others and are the closed optional set. A leaf line is `pointer:wire-type`, so a field that legitimately arrives under two types is two lines and a nullable field is one line plus its `:null`; there is no way to write down `any type`. HOLDOUT: this projection was built from bodies fetched between 03:13Z and 03:25Z and then checked against a body fetched at 03:33Z that contributed nothing to it. That later page promoted. MEASURED SEMANTICS A LEAF LISTING DOES NOT ITSELF CARRY. The document is a BARE top-level JSON array: no envelope, no total, no cursor, so this route asserts nothing about completeness and this review promotes no completeness claim. `limit` SILENTLY CLAMPS TO 70 — 71, 100 and 1000 each returned exactly 70 rows under HTTP 200 with no warning. `offset` pages a population that moves under it at roughly one new coin per second, and stops paying out silently: offset=1000 returned 70 rows while offset=1030, 2000 and 5000 each returned the two bytes `[]` under HTTP 200, so past-the-end and matched-nothing are indistinguishable and an empty page is NEVER evidence that nothing matched. The provider enumerates its own sorts in its 400 body: created_timestamp, market_cap, ath_market_cap, reply_count, last_reply, last_trade_timestamp; `order` is ASC or DESC; `last_reply` is sortable but is not a field this route returns. UNITS HAZARD: created_timestamp, last_trade_timestamp, ath_market_cap_timestamp, king_of_the_hill_timestamp and last_reply are epoch MILLISECONDS while updated_at ALONE is epoch SECONDS; read as milliseconds updated_at lands on 21 January 1970, which reads as a plausible stale record rather than as a units error. TWO FIELDS ASSERT ONE QUANTITY AND DISAGREE: market_cap_usd and usd_market_cap differ on essentially every row, median 0.10 percent and up to 0.31 percent over 140 rows; both are required leaves here and neither may be silently preferred. RESERVES GO STALE ON GRADUATION: a coin with complete=true was observed carrying virtual_sol_reserves=30000000000 and real_sol_reserves=0, the untouched launch constants, while its market cap fell 97 percent in ninety-seven seconds; the reserve quartet is required on this route but it is NOT price-bearing for a graduated coin, which is why crate::reserves refuses to assemble it and the field tags say so. WHAT IS NOT HERE: no volume, no trade count, no holder count, no buy/sell split, and no price at any earlier instant. This review was made by an agent, not by Ember. It authorises retaining and normalizing provider-asserted numbers as provider assertions only; it certifies no price, no executability and no on-chain fact. AMENDED 2026-08-22 04:07Z, v1 -> v2, ON EVIDENCE AND NOT ON INFERENCE. v1 required $/image_uri:string on every row, because all 1308 rows of the 26 bodies v1 reviewed carried one. The very first live sweep run against v1 REFUSED a page: acquisition acq:pump-api:86c985d12d58fd035505a487764cd1f8:1787371612421131-1602f964f0d0548c90617f8cf54aac3f, row 21, mint 3E3bEpbFDxyBy6KDqdBKRAFiLZTn49mG19KAMW1jpump, name "NA", which carries no image_uri, description, metadata_uri, twitter, website or king_of_the_hill_timestamp at all — a coin created with no metadata whatsoever. That page contributed nothing to the ranking and was counted as refused, which is the gate behaving correctly. $/image_uri:string therefore moves from required to optional here, on the strength of that named acquisition, and the leaf listing below is recomputed over 38 bodies and 2014 rows including it. Nothing else moved. AMENDED AGAIN, v2 -> v3, AND THIS TIME THE PRINCIPLE CHANGED RATHER THAN THE OBSERVATIONS. Three separate live pages refused within minutes of v1 shipping, each on a genuinely unobserved provider fact: a coin created with NO metadata at all (mint 3E3bEpbFDxyBy6KDqdBKRAFiLZTn49mG19KAMW1jpump, name "NA") carrying no image_uri; a nested $/mayhem/complete_reason no reviewer had read, seen as {"state":"completed","mode":"auto","complete_reason":"zero_base_amount"}; and a search row for a coin that has never traded, carrying no last_trade_timestamp. Each refusal was correct and each was cheap to resolve, but the pattern showed the required set was being computed wrongly: it was every leaf seen on every row, INCLUDING leaves this crate never reads. Requiring an unread field buys nothing — its absence cannot harm any consumer — and costs a refusal every time the provider omits it on a rare row, which is how a fail-closed gate becomes noise that a tired reader learns to wave through. From v3 the required set is scoped to EXACTLY the projection the normalizer reads, and RowProjectionReviewV1::validate now REFUSES any review that requires a leaf outside that projection. Everything else the provider sends is still in the CLOSED optional set, so an unreviewed leaf still refuses the page: the anti-silent-drop rule is untouched. What changed is that a required-leaf refusal now means a field this codebase actually consumes went missing, which is a fact worth stopping for. A NOTE FOR WHOEVER OPERATES THIS. The required set is an EMPIRICAL claim — leaves present on every row of every body looked at so far — and it will occasionally be refuted by a rarer row. Early operation should expect refusals, and a refusal is a finding rather than a fault: read the named row in the retained bytes, decide whether the leaf really is optional, and amend. It must never be resolved by widening to a shape nobody has read. v3 leaf listing recomputed over 44 live bodies and 2434 rows: 31 required, every one of them a field the normalizer reads, and 36 optional. Leaves present on every row but never read by this crate — hide_banner, is_cashback_enabled, livestream_ban_expiry, show_name — are optional here for that reason and not because they were seen missing.
